entries.problem: Modeless palette windows can close immediately after script execution.
entries.solution: Use #targetengine with a persistent session name before creating palette windows.

entries.problem: Event listeners can run in a different engine context and lose closure state.
entries.solution: Use shared state on persistent engine objects or prefer IdleTask polling for selection monitoring.

entries.problem: The move() by argument can fail when UnitValue objects are passed directly.
entries.solution: Pass numeric offsets or unit strings (for example '10mm') that match InDesign expectations.

entries.problem: geometricBounds is often confused with x,y,width,height.
entries.solution: Always use geometricBounds as [top, left, bottom, right].

entries.problem: Find/change operations can produce incorrect results when preferences are not reset.
entries.solution: Reset find and change preferences to NothingEnum.NOTHING before each find/change operation.

entries.problem: ExtendScript does not support modern JavaScript syntax.
entries.solution: Use ES3-compatible syntax (var, classic functions, string concatenation).

entries.problem: File path handling can fail with raw path assumptions.
entries.solution: Construct file references explicitly with File('/path/file') or File('~/Desktop/file').

entries.problem: Direct indexing into empty collections causes runtime errors.
entries.solution: Check collection.length before reading collection[index].

entries.problem: parentPage is null for items on the pasteboard.
entries.solution: Wrap parentPage access in try/catch or explicit null checks.

entries.problem: Using return instead of __result yields missing or unexpected outputs.
entries.solution: Assign output values to __result and avoid return statements in run_jsx payloads.

entries.problem: Manual loops create unnecessary bridge round-trips for uniform operations.
entries.solution: Use collection APIs (everyItem, itemByName, itemByID, itemByRange) whenever possible.

entries.problem: app.selection cannot contain objects from multiple spreads. Setting app.selection with items across spreads causes errors or unexpected behavior.
entries.solution: When selecting multiple objects programmatically, filter to items on the active spread only. Use item.parentPage or item.parent to determine spread membership, or navigate to each spread individually.

entries.problem: spread.allPageItems throws error "Fehlerzeichenfolge: allPageItems" when spread contains deeply corrupted objects (e.g. NaN transforms from nulled/collapsed page items).
entries.solution: Wrap spread.allPageItems in try/catch. On failure, fall back to spread.pageItems (top-level only) and recursively collect children via item.pageItems.
entries.example_bad: try { items = spread.allPageItems; } catch(e) { items = []; var top = spread.pageItems; for (var i=0; i<top.length; i++) { items.push(top[i]); /* recurse children */ } }

entries.problem: FlexObject children and copies derived from FlexObjects may not register in spread.allPageItems after IDML roundtrip, causing them to disappear in Preview mode while remaining visible in Normal and Overprint Preview.
entries.solution: Workaround: Cut affected top-level item, paste into a temp rectangle, cut it back out, paste back, restore bounds. This forces re-registration in the spread hierarchy. Alternatively export/reimport IDML.

entries.problem: app.rtfImportPreferences and app.importPreferences do not exist in ExtendScript DOM
entries.solution: Use app.wordRTFImportPreferences (WordRTFImportPreference object) for RTF import settings. Key properties: removeFormatting, preserveLocalOverrides, importUnusedStyles, resolveCharacterStyleClash, resolveParagraphStyleClash, useTypographersQuotes, importFootnotes, importEndnotes, convertPageBreaks.

entries.problem: Named import presets from the InDesign UI dialog (e.g. "RTF-Format-löschen-m-Abweich") are not accessible as named objects in the ExtendScript DOM
entries.solution: Named presets are UI-only. They simply set properties on the underlying preference object. Access the preference directly via app.wordRTFImportPreferences, or iterate app.preferences (105 entries) to find it — WordRTFImportPreference is typically at index 18. Read/set properties directly in script instead of referencing preset names.

entries.problem: Import preference objects for common file formats are scattered across different app properties, not unified under one namespace
entries.solution: Use the correct preference object per format: .rtf/.doc → app.wordRTFImportPreferences (removeFormatting, preserveLocalOverrides, resolveCharacterStyleClash, resolveParagraphStyleClash); .txt → app.textImportPreferences (characterSet, platform — critical for correct codepage/encoding); .pdf (place) → app.pdfPlacePreferences (pdfCrop, transparentBackground); .ai/.pdf (page) → app.importedPageAttributes (importedPageCrop); .eps → app.epsImportPreferences (epsProxy, opiComments). TIFF/JPEG/PNG have no dedicated import preference objects — alpha/transparency is handled automatically or via frame properties after placing.

entries.problem: doc.paragraphStyles.itemByName() fails or returns nothing for styles organized in groups; doc.paragraphStyles only contains ungrouped top-level styles
entries.solution: Use doc.allParagraphStyles (or doc.allCharacterStyles) to get all styles including those in groups. These return an array without itemByName() — must search with a for-loop: for (var i=0; i < doc.allParagraphStyles.length; i++) { if (doc.allParagraphStyles[i].name === name) return doc.allParagraphStyles[i]; }

entries.problem: Inserting text at the end of a paragraph via insertionPoints requires knowing that characters[length-1] is the trailing \\r — inserting after it creates a new paragraph instead
entries.solution: Use insertionPoints[characters.length - 1] to place the cursor just before the trailing \\r. Insert \\n (charCode 10) for a forced/soft line break that stays within the same paragraph. Using \\r would create a new paragraph. After insertion, refresh story.paragraphs as the collection is live.

entries.problem: story.paragraphs is a live collection — indices shift immediately after any insert or delete, causing off-by-one errors if the collection is cached
entries.solution: Re-fetch story.paragraphs after every insert or delete operation. For multiple deletions always process bottom-up (highest index first) to avoid index shifts affecting remaining targets. Separate the verification pass (read-only) from the mutation pass (destructive) rather than combining them.

entries.problem: Trying to calculate image placement scale manually via graphic.horizontalScale/verticalScale is unreliable — values depend on current frame size and prior fit operations, leading to wrong dimensions
entries.solution: Use frame.fit(FitOptions.PROPORTIONALLY) first to normalize the image into the frame, then read graphic.geometricBounds to get actual image dimensions in frame coordinates, calculate the scale factor from those, resize the frame to target dimensions, and finish with frame.fit(FitOptions.CONTENT_TO_FRAME). This is more reliable than working with horizontalScale/verticalScale directly.

entries.problem: TextWrapModes enum values are not obvious from the name alone — numeric fallback needed when enum name doesn't resolve in older ExtendScript contexts
entries.solution: TextWrapModes.BOUNDING_BOX_TEXT_WRAP = 1651729523; TextWrapModes.NONE = 1852796517. textWrapOffset takes [top, right, bottom, left] order (like CSS). Always set textWrapMode before textWrapOffset.

entries.problem: RTF files with Windows-1252 encoding (ansicpg1252) can produce garbled characters (placeholder glyphs) when imported into InDesign, even though the RTF header declares the correct codepage
entries.solution: The root cause is usually the system locale or InDesign's RTF parser misinterpreting \'xx hex sequences. Fix via app.wordRTFImportPreferences: ensure the correct settings are applied before placing. If garbling persists despite correct settings, the issue may be in Word's RTF writer (some versions embed characters as \\u sequences instead of \'xx) or a mismatch between the RTF codepage and the actual byte values. Verify by reading the raw RTF bytes in PowerShell with [System.Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(1252) and checking that \'e4 → ä, \'f6 → ö, \'fc → ü etc. The symptom of partial garbling (some words lose letters like "Philharmoniker" → "rmo") points to InDesign treating multi-byte sequences from a wrong font charset declaration in the RTF fonttbl.

entries.problem: Scripting operations planned from stale assumptions (e.g. paragraph indices, existing objects, style names from a previous session) can fail silently or corrupt the document if the state has changed due to undo/redo or prior operations
entries.solution: Always run a read-only JSX verification pass first to confirm current document state before executing any destructive or structural operations. Check: correct document is active (app.activeDocument.name), expected frames exist and have correct column count, paragraph styles are present (doc.allParagraphStyles), existing images are as expected (page.allPageItems with link names). Never carry over index assumptions from previous sessions.

entries.problem: Combining read/verify logic and destructive mutations in a single JSX block makes it hard to detect partial failures and recover — if the destructive part fails mid-way the document can be in an inconsistent state
entries.solution: Split complex text or layout operations into separate JSX calls: (1) read-only verification pass that returns a log of what will be done, (2) the actual mutation pass. Review the plan output between steps when stakes are high. Use undo_mode='entire' on the mutation pass so a single undo reverts everything cleanly. For very complex operations, further split into logical sub-steps each with their own undo label.

entries.problem: Temporary ScriptLabels created during multi-step MCP workflows accumulate in documents and pollute the label namespace, which can mislead later agent runs.
entries.solution: Use a strict label lifecycle: `_tmp_` keys are temporary handoff state and must be deleted at task end via `insertLabel(key, "")`; `agentContext_` keys are only for stable cross-session facts with proven future value. Optionally track persistent keys in `_agentLabelRegistry` for auditability.

entries.problem: doc.swatches returns items as generic Swatch class; instanceof Color fails. color.space returns numeric enum values, not strings.
entries.solution: Use doc.colors to access Color instances directly. Compare space as integer: CS_CMYK=1129142603, CS_HSB=1665684290, CS_LAB=1665941826, CS_RGB=1666336578.

entries.problem: findText fails to match strings containing special spaces (hair space U+200A, thin space U+2009, non-breaking space U+00A0, en space U+2002, etc.) when the search string uses regular ASCII space (U+0020). Common in typographically refined text from layouts, word processors, or RTF imports.
entries.solution: When findText returns 0 results for a string that visually appears in the frame, inspect actual character codes with charCodeAt(). Common culprits: hair space (8198/U+200A), thin space (8201/U+2009), non-breaking space (160/U+00A0), en space (8194/U+2002), figure space (8199/U+2007). Build the search string with String.fromCharCode() for the correct code point. Also watch for: typographic quotes (U+201C/201D/2018/2019), en dash (U+2013), fi/fl ligatures (U+FB01/FB02).

entries.problem: app.bringToFront() does not exist in InDesign ExtendScript — throws error 24 "is not a function".
entries.solution: Use app.activate() instead — this is the correct DOM method to bring InDesign to the foreground before showing a modal dialog.

entries.problem: afterOpen event fires before InDesign completes layout recomposition. Nulled-object scans at this moment report false positives (zero-scale objects that resolve once InDesign stabilizes).
entries.solution: Delay scans triggered by afterOpen using an IdleTask. This ensures transforms are fully resolved before inspection.

entries.problem: Setting frame.previousTextFrame = X when X already has a nextTextFrame Y inserts the frame BETWEEN X and Y rather than disconnecting Y. Subsequently re-assigning frame.nextTextFrame = Y throws 'Invalid object for this request'.
entries.solution: When inserting frames into an existing thread chain, only set previousTextFrame on each new frame in order — do NOT explicitly re-attach the original next-frame at the tail. InDesign auto-shifts the existing nextTextFrame down the chain.
entries.example_bad:
for (var m = 1; m < N; m++) { frames[m].previousTextFrame = frames[m-1]; }
frames[N-1].nextTextFrame = origNext; // throws if origNext was src.nextTextFrame
entries.example_good:
// Drop the tail re-attach — InDesign already chained origNext after frames[N-1]
for (var m = 1; m < N; m++) { frames[m].previousTextFrame = frames[m-1]; }

entries.problem: Folder.getFiles(maskString) treats the argument as a file-system glob, so '/' and '\' are read as PATH SEPARATORS and '[' ']' '*' '?' as wildcards. Passing a user-fed string (e.g. a section marker or label containing slashes) silently matches nothing instead of erroring, breaking file lookups (e.g. version detection that always returns v1 and overwrites existing files).
entries.solution: Never build a getFiles() glob mask from user-controlled strings. Use the predicate form getFiles(function(f){ return regex.test(decodeURI(f.name)); }) with a RegExp built from escapeRegExp() of the sanitized string. Match against decodeURI(f.name), guarded by try/catch so a stray '%' cannot throw.
entries.example_bad:
// Slashes in `identifier` become path separators -> no match -> always v1
var files = Folder(path).getFiles(baseName + '*_' + identifier + '_v*.pdf');

triggers: paragraph style leaks to next paragraph
entries.problem: Overwriting paragraph.contents including its own trailing \r (e.g. p.contents = "new text\r") can cause the paragraph's style to bleed forward onto the NEXT paragraph, corrupting adjacent paragraph styling even though that paragraph's text was untouched. No error is thrown — the corruption is silent.
entries.solution: Never include the trailing \r when replacing a paragraph's text. Replace only the characters before the pilcrow: if (p.characters[len-1].contents === "\r") { p.characters.itemByRange(0, len-2).contents = newText; } This leaves the paragraph-mark/style boundary completely untouched and prevents style bleed to the following paragraph.
entries.example_bad: p.contents = "new text\r"; // may bleed style to next paragraph

entries.problem: Multiple sequential insertParagraphAfter() calls within one run_jsx batch, targeting paragraph object references captured up front (before any insertions ran), land in the wrong position from the 2nd insertion onward — each new paragraph tends to appear one slot too early. The first insertion works correctly; only later ones in the same script drift.
entries.solution: Do not batch multiple structural paragraph insertions targeting different pre-captured paragraph refs in a single run_jsx call. Instead, perform ONE insertion per run_jsx call, re-fetching the target paragraph fresh (e.g. by matching distinctive text content via story.paragraphs loop) immediately before each insertion, and verify placement with a read-only pass before the next insertion.

entries.problem: Scanning and removing characters one by one across all long export stories can leave InDesign unresponsive for minutes and force process termination (MCP request timeouts, Responding=False).
entries.solution: Keep structural edits in a short undo transaction; post-process icon spans in exported HTML rather than in the live document; split threaded stories by capturing the destination frame insertion index, unlinking it, then moving the trailing text range into the new story in one operation.

entries.problem: In UXP scripts, 'app' and InDesign Enums (Justification, UndoModes, ExportFormat, etc.) are not globally available by default.
entries.solution: Always import InDesign DOM objects and Enums explicitly with `const { app, Justification, UndoModes } = require('indesign');` in UXP code.
entries.example_bad: const doc = app.activeDocument; // ReferenceError: app is not defined in UXP
entries.example_good:
const { app } = require('indesign');
const doc = app.activeDocument;

triggers: Die Anforderung kann nicht bearbeitet werden
entries.problem: Unhandled runtime exceptions in UXP scripts can trigger modal InDesign alert dialogs that block subsequent COM/OLE requests with an active modal dialog error.
entries.solution: Always wrap UXP logic in try/catch or use the MCP `run_jsx(..., language='uxp')` wrapper which catches errors safely and serializes structured error messages.

entries.problem: COM app.DoScript(code, ScriptLanguage.UXPSCRIPT) does not return the last evaluated expression value directly, returning None instead.
entries.solution: Assign return data to `__result` so the MCP wrapper serializes it via ScriptLabels, or use explicit insertLabel/extractLabel or ScriptArgs.

entries.problem: Agents may default to UXP assuming newer is always better, but LLM training data for ExtendScript InDesign DOM is far larger and more reliable.
entries.solution: Default to ExtendScript (`language='javascript'`) for 95% of tasks (layout, DOM, styling, table ops). Use UXP (`language='uxp'`) selectively for complex data transformations (Array map/filter/reduce, Set, Map, async data loops), or native JSON handling.

entries.problem: Calling `setTimeout()`, `setInterval()`, or `fetch()` inside standalone UXP scripts via COM/DoScript does not resolve because InDesign's main-thread macrotask event loop is not pumped during synchronous execution, causing scripts to time out.
entries.solution: Do not rely on macrotask timers (`setTimeout`/`setInterval`) or `fetch()` inside InDesign UXP scripts. Use synchronous/microtask async code (`Promise.resolve`, `Promise.all`, async computation). Perform timers and HTTP requests in the external agent/Python layer.

entries.problem: run_jsx fails with 'Die Anforderung kann nicht bearbeitet werden, da ein modales Dialogfeld oder eine modale Warnmeldung aktiv ist' (COMError from COM/DoScript) while a native InDesign dialog is open, for example a profile/policy mismatch, a multi-document open progress window, or a ScriptUI report. The dialog is often hidden behind other windows.
entries.solution: Do not retry run_jsx until the modal is dismissed. Identify the blocker by enumerating visible top-level window titles owned by the InDesign process, bring that window forward, dismiss it, then re-run run_jsx. app.activate() can surface InDesign but does not close the dialog. Dismiss via UI automation only with user consent.

entries.problem: Opening many documents shows one 'Abweichung von Profil oder Richtlinie' dialog per document whose embedded profile does not match the working space. Each dialog blocks all COM scripting until it is answered.
entries.solution: When the agent opens the files, set app.colorSettings.mismatchAskWhenOpening = false before the batch and restore the previous value afterwards. If the dialogs are already open, 'Dokument nicht ändern' is the default selection, so confirming OK applies that choice. Dismiss each dialog before the next run_jsx call.

entries.problem: IdleTasks, including ones scheduled by a startup-script afterOpen handler, may not fire while InDesign is in the background. Their sleep stays at the scheduled value, so dependent logic such as pending counters and reports stalls.
entries.solution: When verifying idle-task-driven scripts, read app.idleTasks.everyItem().name and app.idleTasks.everyItem().sleep, then bring InDesign to the foreground with app.activate(). Pending tasks then fire within seconds. A missing report is not evidence of zero findings while app.idleTasks.length is still greater than zero.

entries.problem: Collapsed text after crash recovery during a simultaneous PDF export: frames, matrices, and story text are intact, and an IDML export of the text matches, but every line has zero width, all glyphs sit on one point, and baselines fall outside the frame, so pages look empty. recompose(), ignoreWrap, duplicate(), and nudging the frame leave it broken; a nudge can push the text into overset.
entries.solution: The damage sits in the binary composition cache of the .indd. Detect a line when the distance between its first and last character in x and y is below 0.01 (sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)); an x-only test false-positives on 90-degree rotated frames. Export the affected top-level object with exportFile(ExportFormat.INDESIGN_SNIPPET, file), place it with spread.place(file, [bounds[1], bounds[0]], layer) so the point is [left, top], then call bringToFront(oldItem) on the placed item (reference must share the parent). Rethread partial story chains and point each existing Hyperlink.source at the orphan source the snippet created: snippets carry sources and do not carry hyperlinks. Remove the old object. A full IDML round trip also clears the cache and can rebreak unrelated paragraphs.

entries.problem: Heavy DOM work on a document opened with app.open(file, false) (showingWindow false) can hang InDesign with no dialog and flat CPU. The same code on the same file opened in a window finishes. A long run_jsx call can also exceed the bridge timeout while InDesign keeps running.
entries.solution: Open repair documents with a window: app.open(file, true). Suppress dialogs via app.scriptPreferences.userInteractionLevel = UserInteractionLevels.NEVER_INTERACT and restore the previous value afterwards. For long jobs, open the progress log, writeln one step, and close it each time; a File left open flushes on close. Close only the documents the script opened.

entries.problem: In JSX sent through run_jsx/DoScript, a string literal containing U+FEFF (the \uFEFF escape or the character itself) evaluates to an empty string. Comparisons, indexOf, and split against story text that contains U+FEFF PDF-comment anchors then fail, and split on that empty string splits every character.
entries.solution: Build the character at runtime with String.fromCharCode(0xFEFF). In generated data, store a placeholder such as \u0001 and replace that placeholder with the runtime character before comparing.
entries.example_good:
var FEFF = String.fromCharCode(0xFEFF);
var parts = text.split(FEFF);

entries.problem: While the user keeps working in InDesign, app.activeDocument can change to another open document between run_jsx calls. Reading toxic null hyperlink.destination can also open a foreign document mid-script and switch activeDocument. The undo tool calls undo() on app.activeDocument only, so it can report steps_undone 0 or undo the wrong file.
entries.solution: In every run_jsx, address the target with app.documents.itemByName("file.indd") or by full path. Roll back with that document's undo(), or with an explicit inverse edit, while another document may be active. Leave close_unexpected_documents at its default (true). It only closes foreign documents that are saved and unmodified; modified or untitled ones stay open and the result carries a `warning`. When a result has a `warning`, stop and verify the host before the next edit. See also toxic-null-hyperlink-opens-origin-document.

entries.problem: Assigning characters.itemByRange(a, b).contents keeps the original per-position style runs, so italic or colored words land on unrelated characters of the new string. Inserted text can also inherit local font overrides from the following paragraph.
entries.solution: After the replace, call applyCharacterStyle(style) with the character style of the first original character. The method takes only the style. Clear leftover local formatting with clearOverrides(OverrideType.CHARACTER_ONLY), then re-apply intended emphasis. Verify with textStyleRanges.everyItem().getElements(). The style name on a font is Font.fontStyleName.

entries.problem: After a corruption crash, master items are invisible on specific pages while appliedMaster and masterPageItems look complete, spread.showMasterItems is true, the master page transform is identity, and the IDML OverrideList is empty. Remove all local overrides stays greyed out. Re-applying the master, nudging the master item, and moving the spread leave the pages blank. masterItem.override(page) returns a local copy with zero-area geometricBounds at the spread center.
entries.solution: The per-page master instance is broken and travels with the Page. Replace the spread: add a spread after the old one, copy allowPageShuffle and showMasterItems from the old spread, set appliedMaster on each new page, move old.pageItems from back to front onto the new spread, retarget HyperlinkPageDestination.destinationPage, remove the old spread, and recreate any section that started on a removed page with the same properties. Verify page names, counts, and stacking within 0.05 mm. To scan, call override(page) and read bounds inside doScript(UndoModes.ENTIRE_SCRIPT), then undo. Skip Guides: masterPageItems includes them, and Guide has no geometricBounds.

entries.problem: spread.pageItems, page.pageItems, and everyItem().getElements() are grouped by object type (rectangles, graphic lines, polygons, text frames, groups). PageItem.index is the index within that type. Moving items to another spread in that order re-stacks each layer by type, so a background rectangle can land in front of its text frame. Comparing pageItems order before and after does not show the change.
entries.solution: Read z-order from spread.allPageItems filtered to items whose parent is that spread. The list is front to back, layer by layer. Enforce it by iterating from the back and calling item.bringToFront() with no reference; the call stays on the item's layer. bringToFront(reference) requires the same parent. Verify with the allPageItems id sequence. If allPageItems throws on corrupted items, this read is unavailable.

entries.problem: Copied Hyperlink objects can retain a hidden cross-document provenance after their destination becomes missing (API: hyperlink.destination === null; UI red flag). Reading .destination or calling showDestination() then opens the origin document and may switch activeDocument. This is not HyperlinkExternalPageDestination. Fresh hyperlinks created with hyperlinks.add(source) and no destination are clean nulls and do not open another file. Assigning NothingEnum.NOTHING to destination throws.
entries.solution: Never read `.destination` in a loop without protection. Use the shared core: `$.evalFile(File(Folder.userData + "/Adobe/InDesign/Version 21.0/de_DE/Scripts/Scripts Panel/_lib/toxicHyperlinks.jsxinc")); THL.scan(doc)` (read-only, undo_mode none) and `THL.sanitize(doc, ids, "clean-null")` (one undo step) to rebuild toxic links as clean nulls. The core pins open documents by id, closes only foreign documents that appeared during a probe and are unmodified, suppresses open dialogs and re-activates the host. If you must write your own loop: snapshot document ids before the read, close only new unmodified ones, and address the host by name/id afterwards, never by activeDocument. Repair = remove hyperlink + source, recreate with hyperlinks.add(source) (clean null) or add(source, knownDest) when the real target is known from a side channel. Never invent a URL from link text. Assigning NothingEnum.NOTHING to destination throws. Limitation: if the origin document is already open, probing opens nothing and the link looks like a clean null (THL reports it in nullOnly). run_jsx closes saved, unmodified foreign documents after the script and returns a `warning` when any foreign document appeared.

entries.problem: Each run_jsx call runs in a fresh script engine. Globals, $.global members and libraries loaded with $.evalFile in one call do not exist in the next call. Symptom: 'undefined is not an object' when calling a library function loaded earlier.
entries.solution: Load libraries with $.evalFile(File(absolutePath)) at the top of every run_jsx call that uses them. Pass state between calls as returned data (__result) or document labels, not as globals.
